div.head: Wi 1
div.ab: Die Kirche [sei] in Freiheit von Abgaben;
The Church [is to be] in freedom from taxes;
The Church shall enjoy immunity from taxation.
The Church [is to be] free from taxation.
Freedom of the church from taxation [is to be];

note.seg: Ellipse des sy ist häufig; z. B. Abt 8. II As 14, 2
Ellipsis of sy is frequent; e.g. Abt 8. II As 14, 2

Den Sinn ändert nicht die Auffassung der Worte als ciriccan (wie 2): ‘der Kirche Freiheit’; zu ergänzen ‘gebe mau’; so Toller 334. Freolsdome wäre no. oder acc. mit unorganischem -e der Endung; s. Wb 56. Grimm nimmt ciricean als Acc.: ‘sie mehrten [aus Prol. 3¹ falsch übersetzt und hier unmöglicherweise ergänzt] die K. mit Freiheit’. — Man könnte freols do me vermuten, da him doð munde: ei dant patrocinium II Em 1, 1 bedeutet, und me im 12. Jh von H modernisiert für man sein könnte. Allein letzteres ist bedenklich, und die Wortstellung des Verbs zwischen Objekt und dem von diesem abhängigen Genetiv wohl unmöglich. — Unglücklich ist auch die Erklärung freols dome ⁊ gafole ‘freedom in [!] jurisdiction [!] and revenue [!]’ (Stubbs Councils III 233); dies erfordert drei unbelegte Bedeutungen und nimmt sachlich zu weitgehende Immunität an; s. Gl Geistliches Gericht 16. a. — Die Präpos. an (s. Wb 163 Ac 8) drückt hier wie oft die Lage aus: ‘unter’ mundbyrde, griðe (aaO); das Wort freolsdom; zwar sonst unbezeugt, ist in den auch sonst gut belegten Gliedern wie der Kompositionsart unbedenklich

The meaning is not changed by taking the words as ciriccan (as in 2): ‘the church’s freedom’, with ‘let one give’ to be supplied; so Toller 334. Freolsdome would be nom. or acc. with an inorganic ending -e; see Wb 56. Grimm takes ciricean as acc.: ‘they increased [mistranslated from Prol. 3¹ and impossibly supplied here] the church with freedom’. — One might conjecture freols do me, since him doð munde means ei dant patrocinium II Em 1, 1, and me could have been modernised by H in the 12th cent. for man. But the latter is doubtful, and the position of the verb between the object and the genitive dependent on it is probably impossible. — Also infelicitous is the explanation freols dome ⁊ gafole ‘freedom in [!] jurisdiction [!] and revenue [!]’ (Stubbs Councils III 233); this requires three unattested meanings and assumes an immunity that is too far-reaching in substance; see Gl Geistliches Gericht 16. a. — The preposition an (see Wb 163 Ac 8) here, as often, expresses situation: ‘under’ mundbyrde, griðe (loc. cit.); the word freolsdom, though otherwise unattested, is unobjectionable both in its elements, which are well attested elsewhere, and in its manner of composition

Vgl. Gl Kirchenfreiheit 2. Der Satz hebt die Trinoda necessitas (s. Gl) nicht notwendig auf. Ein ius regium generale in universis terris ecclesiasticis in Cantia stand 732 fest; Bi 148; vgl. Bright Chapters of church hist. 382. Eine späte Überarbeitung der Synode von Bapchild dehnt die dort auf bestimmte Stifter beschränkte Freiheit auch von Staatsfronden auf alle Kirchen Englands aus: vielleicht aus Wi 1. Wäre unser Satz eine Wirklichkeit, das Kirchenprivileg allgemein giltig geworden, so hätte es Wihtræd nicht erst laut des (nach Earle Landchart. 44) echten Kernes von Bapchild seinen Stiftern im besonderen zuzuwenden nötig gefunden. Der Satz war also vielleicht nur predigender Wunsch

Cf. Gl Kirchenfreiheit 2. The clause does not necessarily abolish the Trinoda necessitas (see Gl). A ius regium generale in universis terris ecclesiasticis in Cantia was firmly established in 732; Bi 148; cf. Bright Chapters of church hist. 382. A late reworking of the synod of Bapchild extends to all the churches of England the freedom, there restricted to particular foundations, which included freedom from public labour services: perhaps on the basis of Wi 1. If our clause had been a reality, and the church’s privilege had become generally valid, Wihtræd would not have found it necessary first to confer it on his foundations in particular, as he does according to the (after Earle Landchart. 44) genuine core of Bapchild. The clause was therefore perhaps only a homiletic wish

note.label: freolsdome
note.seg: anfreols dome. H. Schmid, following Wilkins, writes Ciricean freolsdome; Liebermann, as above.
sc. sie; literally, ‘the Church shall be in freedom of,’ etc.

note.label: gafola;
note.seg: Manuscript spacing is Cirice anfreols dome gafola. See note e to translation.

note.label: be];
note.seg: This clause is grammatically somewhat problematic, although the import is clear. The spacing of the manuscript makes no sense (see note c to the Old English text); as most previous editors, I have chosen Ciricean. This could be genitive (as translated above) or dative, the latter giving a reading of ‘To the church is to be freedom from taxation’ (literally ‘of tributes’). Note, however, that the next clause begins with a genitival ciricean, which has governed my choice. The difficulty is that freolsdome is in the dative case; both of the proposed readings presuppose an emendation to freolsdom. If one were to edit the phrase Cirice an freolsdome gafola, ‘One church [is to be] with freedom from taxation,’ no emendation would be necessary, but the translation is nonsensical in the absence of competing church religions. (Even more unlikely is the supposition that the clause might refer to a single specific church.) It is also on the threshold of ungrammaticality to have the numeral following the noun. See discussion in Liebermann, Gesetze, 3:26.
